subject: Reserved capacity commit term — pricing sensitivity and approval path
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@acmeai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procurement@acmeai.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool pricing & term — initial ask

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited about trialing Redwood Dedicated for inference on our recommender models. Before we lock infra in, procurement asked me to confirm a few things so they can map to our internal P&L: 

1) Can you send a short sensitivity of committed-term vs unit GPU cost (12 / 24 / 36 months) and what discount tiers you can offer at each length?
2) If we commit to a reserved pool today, what is the realistic lead time to guaranteed capacity (in weeks) and what are SKU/instance constraints?
3) Are there any approval thresholds we should expect (e.g., discounts that require exec sign-off)?

We'd like to understand the downside if GPU spot prices increase over the next 12 months — do you provide automatic re-routing or a price-protection mechanism?

Can you loop in finance/ops on your side? Procurement would like something they can attach to our internal approval packet by EOW.

Best,
Emma
Emma Liu
Head of Infrastructure 
Acme AI

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool pricing & term — initial ask

Emma — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. Attached is a concise proposal (RDW_commit_proposal_v2.pdf) and a small CSV with sensitivity runs (pricing-sensitivity.csv). High level summary here: 

- Lead times: we can guarantee initial reserved capacity within 6-8 weeks for standard A100/RTX-class SKUs in us-west. Specialized SKUs (H100) may be 10-14 weeks depending on supply.
- Pricing: baseline on-demand equivalent unit cost is used as a reference. Typical committed discounts we offer are 
  * 12 months: ~10-15%
  * 24 months: ~18-24%
  * 36 months: ~25-32%
Discounts depend on committed vCPU/GPU count, burst allowances, and whether customer wants fixed-availability vs flexible (cross-region) pools.
- Approval thresholds: any single-deal discount greater than 30% requires VP-level approval (we'll loop in pricing ops). Any deal that includes cross-region guaranteed capacity with fixed SLAs beyond 36 months will need legal + product sign-off.

I copied Ben and Marissa to validate margin math and approval path. Notes in the PDF: SKU mix recommendations for Acme's workload (mix of medium-latency recs + occasional long-context batches) and a proposal for a staged ramp: 50% commit for first 90 days, review usage after Q4, then scale to full commit by month 6.

Attachments: RDW_commit_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal), pricing-sensitivity.csv (3 scenario table)

Next step: if procurement is comfortable, can you confirm a target commit size (GPUs) and preferred term and I'll get a formal SOW + DocuSign link ready.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Proposed discount bands + operational notes (Acme)

Folks — quick internal note on the Acme ask. I reviewed the numbers in the proposal and pricing-sensitivity.csv. A few operational points to call out before we send anything upstream: 

- We should avoid offering >28% discount on standard SKUs unless there is a firm commit to a 36-month term + minimum monthly drawdown. Anything between 24-28% should require Director approval (Karthik), >28% requires VP sign-off.
- GPU procurement lead-times are sticky. If Acme wants H100 everywhere in their pool, we need to queue orders immediately — that locks BOM and reduces flexibility. For 24-month terms I recommend a mixed SKU (70% A100-equivalent, 30% H100) to protect delivery schedules and reduce cost volatility exposure.
- Proposed contingency: allow 10% burst credit that lets them exceed committed baseline for short windows charged at a mid-level rate (not on-demand). This reduces churn risk during busy periods and helps them avoid over-committing.

Action items: 
- Marissa: confirm P&L margin floor for a deal of this size (we're looking at ~120 GPUs initial).
- Olga: if Acme confirms 24 months + 120 GPUs, I'll draft the approval memo for Karthik and the Director of Pricing.

-ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Dedicated

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Proposed discount bands + operational notes (Acme)

Thanks Ben — see attached my working model (commit-model.xlsx). Key points from finance: 

- Margin floor: for a 24-month baseline with 120 GPUs and our current cost structure, we need at least a 20% blended discount to hit acceptable gross margin after overhead and support (this assumes mixed SKU with 30% premium SKUs).
- Price-protection: we cannot guarantee upstream GPU market prices; however, we can offer a contractual 'cap' on the price-once their pool is provisioned for the first 12 months. After that, the contract will include a quarterly review clause that allows adjustments if 1) global GPU hardware costs rise >15% or 2) power/colocation increases exceed 10% — adjustments are capped to X% (see sheet 'adjustments').
- Accounting: longer terms favor capital recognition and reduce monthly unit cost, but also increase our capital commitment. Finance requires a quarterly variance report tied to the committed drawdown; if utilization falls below 60% for two consecutive quarters, there will be an automatic review and potential repricing clause.

If Acme is comfortable with these protections and a 24-month term with 20% discount, I'll prepare the finance addendum for the SOW and route for approval. Otherwise, I can run 12/36-month scenarios in the same model — let me know which to prioritize.

Attachments: commit-model.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@acmeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity commit term — pricing sensitivity and approval path

Emma — thanks for the patience while we ran the numbers with finance and pricing. Recap and recommendation based on Acme's stated profile and the sensitivity models we ran: 

1) Recommended term & discount: 24 months with a 20% blended discount (mixed SKU: 70% A100-equivalent, 30% H100). This keeps us above finance margin floor and gives Acme meaningful cost predictability.
2) Lead time & operational plan: we can provision an initial confirmed pool of 120 GPUs in ~8 weeks (standard SKUs) with a staged ramp: 60 GPUs live at T+6 weeks, +60 GPUs at T+12 weeks. H100 proportion will depend on final ordering window; if Acme wants 50% H100 we need to sign within 7 days to meet procurement windows.
3) Protections & clauses: we will include a 12-month price cap on hardware-related unit costs, quarterly review triggers for large cost changes (as Marissa outlined), and a utilization clause (review if <60% for two consecutive quarters).
4) Approval path: Discounts up to 24% can be approved by Director (Karthik). Anything >28% will need VP sign-off. For this recommended 20% band, we'll proceed with Director-level routing only.

Next steps: 
- If Acme confirms the 24-month / 120 GPU target, I will issue an SOW + DocuSign envelope (link to follow).
- Internal: Ben will prepare the short approval memo for Karthik and Director pricing. Marissa will attach the finance addendum to the SOW.

Quoted for transparency: "If you confirm a 24-month term with the mixed SKU proposal within seven days, we can hold our proposed H100 allocation and targeted lead times."

Looking forward — I can set up a 30-minute procurement sync this week to finalize details.

Best regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
